blocks.en: Genesis Intensive — Unit 6: Abraham — Called by Grace
blocks.es_reference: Intensivo de Génesis — Unidad 6: Abraham — Llamado por Gracia

blocks.en: “I will bless you and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing.” — Genesis 12:2 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: “Y te bendeciré, y engrandeceré tu nombre, y serás bendición.” — Génesis 12:2 (RVG)

blocks.en: A New Beginning in Genesis 12
blocks.es_reference: Un Nuevo Comienzo en Génesis 12

blocks.en: Genesis 1–11 moves through creation, Fall, judgment, preservation, nations, and Babel. At Genesis 12 the story narrows dramatically to one man, Abram, but God’s purpose does not become narrow. The call of Abram is God’s gracious response within a world still marked by sin and scattering. The promise given to one family has the nations in view from the beginning: “in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.” The patriarchal story therefore begins with grace and mission, not with ethnic privilege as an end in itself.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 1–11 recorre la creación, la Caída, el juicio, la preservación, las naciones y Babel. En Génesis 12 la historia se reduce de manera drástica a un solo hombre, Abram, pero el propósito de Dios no se reduce. El llamado de Abram es la respuesta de gracia de Dios en un mundo todavía marcado por el pecado y la dispersión. La promesa dada a una sola familia tiene a las naciones a la vista desde el principio: «serán benditas en ti todas las familias de la tierra». Por tanto, la historia de los patriarcas comienza con la gracia y la misión, no con un privilegio étnico como fin en sí mismo.

blocks.en: Chosen by Grace
blocks.es_reference: Escogido por Gracia

blocks.en: Joshua 24:2 remembers that Abraham’s family background was associated with the worship of other gods. Nothing in that background suggests that Abram earned the call by possessing superior spiritual credentials. God initiates. The biblical Abraham will become a remarkable example of faith, but he begins as the recipient of grace rather than its source. This protects the course from turning Abraham into a self-made religious hero and keeps the almighty God at the center of the narrative.
blocks.es_reference: Josué 24:2 recuerda que el trasfondo familiar de Abraham estaba ligado al culto a otros dioses. Nada en ese trasfondo sugiere que Abram se ganara el llamado por tener credenciales espirituales superiores. Dios toma la iniciativa. El Abraham bíblico llegará a ser un ejemplo notable de fe, pero comienza como receptor de la gracia y no como su fuente. Esto impide que el curso convierta a Abraham en un héroe religioso hecho a sí mismo y mantiene al Dios todopoderoso en el centro del relato.

blocks.en: The Call to Go
blocks.es_reference: El Llamado a Salir

blocks.en: God calls Abram to leave country, kindred, and his father’s house for a land God will show him. Faith therefore requires movement before Abram possesses the full map. Yet biblical faith is not irrational willingness to follow any strong inward impression. Abram responds to the God who speaks and promises. Christian application must preserve that distinction: believers may obey God without knowing every future detail, but private impulses should still be tested by Scripture, wisdom, character, and the responsibilities God has already made clear.
blocks.es_reference: Dios llama a Abram a dejar su tierra, su parentela y la casa de su padre, e ir a una tierra que Dios le mostrará. Así, la fe exige ponerse en marcha antes de que Abram tenga el mapa completo. Sin embargo, la fe bíblica no es una disposición irracional a seguir cualquier impresión interior intensa. Abram responde al Dios que habla y promete. La aplicación cristiana debe conservar esa distinción: los creyentes pueden obedecer a Dios sin conocer cada detalle del futuro, pero los impulsos personales deben seguir sometiéndose a prueba a la luz de la Escritura, la sabiduría, el carácter y las responsabilidades que Dios ya ha dejado claras.

blocks.en: Babel’s Name and Abraham’s Name
blocks.es_reference: El Nombre de Babel y el Nombre de Abraham

blocks.en: The placement after Babel is important. Babel’s builders say, “let us make a name for ourselves,” while God tells Abram, “I will bless you and make your name great.” Human beings at Babel attempt to manufacture security and significance in proud independence; Abram receives significance as gift and calling. The issue is not whether a person is known or influential. The issue is whether life is organized around self-exaltation or around receiving God’s grace and becoming a blessing to others.
blocks.es_reference: Su ubicación después de Babel es importante. Los constructores de Babel dicen: «hagámonos un nombre», mientras que Dios dice a Abram: «te bendeciré, y engrandeceré tu nombre». En Babel, los seres humanos intentan fabricarse seguridad e importancia con orgullosa independencia; Abram recibe la importancia como un don y un llamamiento. La cuestión no es si una persona es conocida o influyente. La cuestión es si la vida se organiza en torno a la autoexaltación o en torno a recibir la gracia de Dios y llegar a ser de bendición para los demás.

blocks.en: The Threefold Promise
blocks.es_reference: La Promesa Triple

blocks.en: Genesis 12 introduces promises that will govern the patriarchal story: land, descendants, and blessing. Abram will become a great nation, receive God’s blessing, and become a channel through whom blessing reaches others. These promises unfold gradually and sometimes through circumstances that appear to contradict them. Their fulfillment depends finally upon God’s faithfulness, not Abraham’s flawless performance. The remainder of Genesis repeatedly tests whether the reader will trust the promise-giving God when visible circumstances are incomplete.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 12 presenta promesas que regirán la historia de los patriarcas: la tierra, la descendencia y la bendición. Abram llegará a ser una gran nación, recibirá la bendición de Dios y será el canal por medio del cual la bendición alcanzará a otros. Estas promesas se van cumpliendo poco a poco y, a veces, a través de circunstancias que parecen contradecirlas. Su cumplimiento depende, en definitiva, de la fidelidad de Dios y no de un desempeño impecable de Abraham. El resto de Génesis pone a prueba una y otra vez si el lector confiará en el Dios que promete cuando lo que se ve todavía está incompleto.

blocks.en: Blessed to Become a Blessing
blocks.es_reference: Bendecido para Ser Bendición

blocks.en: The words “you shall be a blessing” prevent the promise from becoming merely private prosperity. God’s gifts carry vocation. Abraham is blessed so that blessing may move outward, and Genesis 12:3 places all the families of the earth within that horizon. The same principle challenges churches and individual believers who think of grace only in terms of what they receive. God’s favor creates responsibility for service, generosity, witness, and mission.
blocks.es_reference: Las palabras «serás bendición» impiden que la promesa se convierta simplemente en prosperidad privada. Los dones de Dios traen consigo una vocación. Abraham es bendecido para que la bendición se extienda hacia afuera, y Génesis 12:3 sitúa a todas las familias de la tierra dentro de ese horizonte. El mismo principio desafía a las iglesias y a los creyentes que piensan en la gracia solo en términos de lo que reciben. El favor de Dios crea una responsabilidad de servicio, generosidad, testimonio y misión.

blocks.en: Faith Expressed in Obedience
blocks.es_reference: Fe Expresada en Obediencia

blocks.en: Genesis 12:4 states simply that Abram departed as the LORD had spoken to him. The obedience is significant because the call is costly and the destination is not yet possessed. Faith is not mere agreement with propositions about God; genuine trust changes direction. At the same time, obedience should not be treated as payment that purchases grace. Abram obeys because God has called and promised. Grace initiates, faith receives, and obedience gives visible expression to that trust.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 12:4 dice sencillamente que Abram se fue como Jehová le había dicho. Esa obediencia es significativa porque el llamado es costoso y el destino todavía no le pertenece. La fe no es un simple asentimiento a ciertas afirmaciones acerca de Dios; la confianza genuina cambia el rumbo. Al mismo tiempo, la obediencia no debe tratarse como un pago con el que se compra la gracia. Abram obedece porque Dios lo ha llamado y le ha prometido. La gracia toma la iniciativa, la fe recibe y la obediencia da expresión visible a esa confianza.

blocks.en: Tents and Altars
blocks.es_reference: Tiendas y Altares

blocks.en: As Abram moves through the land, two images repeatedly characterize his life: tents and altars. The tent reflects his status as one who has not yet received settled possession of the promise; the altar reflects worship of the God who has promised. Hebrews later describes Abraham as a stranger and pilgrim looking beyond immediate possession. The combination is spiritually instructive. Faith can live without possessing everything it has been promised because worship anchors the pilgrim in the faithfulness of God.
blocks.es_reference: A medida que Abram recorre la tierra, dos imágenes caracterizan una y otra vez su vida: las tiendas y los altares. La tienda refleja su condición de alguien que todavía no ha recibido la posesión estable de lo prometido; el altar refleja la adoración al Dios que ha prometido. Más tarde, Hebreos describe a Abraham como extranjero y peregrino que mira más allá de la posesión inmediata. Esta combinación es espiritualmente instructiva. La fe puede vivir sin poseer aún todo lo que se le ha prometido, porque la adoración ancla al peregrino en la fidelidad de Dios.

blocks.en: The Famine and the Failure in Egypt
blocks.es_reference: El Hambre y el Fracaso en Egipto

blocks.en: Soon after the call, famine drives Abram toward Egypt, and fear exposes weakness in the man of faith. He presents Sarai as his sister in a way that places her at risk and protects himself. Genesis does not hide the failure of its central human characters. The chosen man can act fearfully, and God’s promise continues not because Abraham never fails but because God remains faithful. Grace should never be confused with approval of Abraham’s deception; Scripture can show divine faithfulness while honestly exposing human sin.
blocks.es_reference: Poco después del llamado, el hambre empuja a Abram hacia Egipto, y el temor deja al descubierto la debilidad del hombre de fe. Presenta a Sarai como su hermana de una manera que la pone en peligro a ella y lo protege a él. Génesis no oculta los fracasos de sus personajes humanos principales. El hombre escogido puede actuar por temor, y la promesa de Dios sigue adelante no porque Abraham nunca falle, sino porque Dios permanece fiel. La gracia nunca debe confundirse con la aprobación del engaño de Abraham; la Escritura puede mostrar la fidelidad divina y, al mismo tiempo, exponer con honestidad el pecado humano.

blocks.en: Returning to the Altar
blocks.es_reference: Regreso al Altar

blocks.en: Genesis 13 brings Abram back to the place where he had previously built an altar, and there he again calls on the name of the LORD. Failure does not have to become the final chapter of a believer’s life. The narrative does not romanticize the failure, but neither does it make restoration impossible. A life of faith includes returning to God after fear and bad judgment have led us away from faithful conduct. Grace restores without pretending that the wrong was right.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 13 lleva a Abram de regreso al lugar donde antes había edificado un altar, y allí vuelve a invocar el nombre de Jehová. El fracaso no tiene por qué ser el capítulo final en la vida de un creyente. El relato no idealiza el fracaso, pero tampoco hace imposible la restauración. Una vida de fe incluye volver a Dios después de que el temor y el mal juicio nos han apartado de una conducta fiel. La gracia restaura sin fingir que lo malo estuvo bien.

blocks.en: Abraham and Lot
blocks.es_reference: Abraham y Lot

blocks.en: Conflict develops because Abram’s and Lot’s possessions have become too great for them to remain together in the same area. Abram gives Lot freedom to choose, and Lot selects the well-watered Jordan plain. The New Testament later describes Lot as a righteous man, so he should not be reduced to a cartoon villain. Yet Genesis 13 also shows the danger of choices governed primarily by visible advantage while moral danger is minimized. Abram can release the apparently better land because his future finally rests in God’s promise rather than in securing the best-looking opportunity.
blocks.es_reference: Surge un conflicto porque las posesiones de Abram y de Lot han llegado a ser demasiado grandes para que puedan seguir juntos en la misma zona. Abram deja que Lot escoja, y Lot elige la llanura del Jordán, bien regada. Más tarde, el Nuevo Testamento describe a Lot como un hombre justo, así que no debe reducirse a un villano de caricatura. Sin embargo, Génesis 13 también muestra el peligro de las decisiones guiadas principalmente por la ventaja visible, mientras se resta importancia al peligro moral. Abram puede renunciar a la tierra que parece mejor porque, en definitiva, su futuro descansa en la promesa de Dios y no en asegurarse la oportunidad más atractiva.

blocks.en: The Promise Reaffirmed
blocks.es_reference: La Promesa Reafirmada

blocks.en: After Lot separates from him, God again tells Abram to look over the land and repeats the promise of descendants and possession. The timing matters. Abram has just surrendered the first choice of territory, yet God reminds him that the promise cannot be lost through generosity. Faith does not have to grasp anxiously at every advantage. The God who calls is capable of sustaining what He has promised.
blocks.es_reference: Después de que Lot se separa de él, Dios vuelve a decir a Abram que contemple la tierra y le repite la promesa de descendencia y posesión. El momento es significativo. Abram acaba de ceder la primera opción sobre el territorio, pero Dios le recuerda que la promesa no puede perderse por ser generoso. La fe no tiene que aferrarse con ansiedad a cada ventaja. El Dios que llama es capaz de sostener lo que ha prometido.

blocks.en: Abram the Rescuer
blocks.es_reference: Abram el Rescatador

blocks.en: Genesis 14 shows Abram acting decisively when Lot is captured in war. He mobilizes his household, pursues the captors, and rescues Lot and the others. Faith is not passivity. The same man who yielded land to avoid unnecessary conflict can act courageously when another person needs rescue. Biblical peaceableness and moral courage belong together; refusing selfish conflict does not mean refusing responsible action.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 14 muestra a Abram actuando con decisión cuando Lot es capturado en una guerra. Moviliza a los hombres de su casa, persigue a los captores y rescata a Lot y a los demás. La fe no es pasividad. El mismo hombre que cedió tierra para evitar un conflicto innecesario puede actuar con valentía cuando otra persona necesita ser rescatada. El espíritu pacífico que enseña la Biblia y el valor moral van juntos; rechazar los conflictos egoístas no significa rechazar la acción responsable.

blocks.en: Melchizedek and the Blessing of God Most High
blocks.es_reference: Melquisedec y la Bendición del Dios Altísimo

blocks.en: After the victory Abram meets Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High. Melchizedek blesses Abram and blesses God, declaring that God delivered Abram’s enemies into his hand. Abram gives him a tenth. Later Scripture, especially Hebrews, develops Melchizedek in relation to Christ’s priesthood, but Genesis 14 already redirects attention away from Abram’s military skill toward God Most High as the giver of victory and blessing.
blocks.es_reference: Después de la victoria, Abram se encuentra con Melquisedec, rey de Salem y sacerdote del Dios Altísimo. Melquisedec bendice a Abram y bendice a Dios, declarando que Dios entregó a los enemigos de Abram en su mano. Abram le da el diezmo. La Escritura posterior, especialmente Hebreos, desarrolla la figura de Melquisedec en relación con el sacerdocio de Cristo, pero ya Génesis 14 aparta la atención de la habilidad militar de Abram y la dirige al Dios Altísimo como el que da la victoria y la bendición.

blocks.en: Refusing the King of Sodom’s Reward
blocks.es_reference: Rechazando la Recompensa del Rey de Sodoma

blocks.en: Abram refuses to enrich himself from the king of Sodom, explaining that he does not want the king to say, “I have made Abram rich.” The decision fits the larger theology of his call. Abram’s future is to rest in God’s blessing rather than in an arrangement that could compromise the witness of that dependence. This is not a universal rule that believers must refuse all compensation or business relationships. It is a narrative example of guarding integrity when a legitimate-looking gain could distort allegiance or testimony.
blocks.es_reference: Abram se niega a enriquecerse con los bienes del rey de Sodoma, y explica que no quiere que el rey diga: «Yo enriquecí a Abram». Esta decisión concuerda con la teología más amplia de su llamado. El futuro de Abram debe descansar en la bendición de Dios y no en un arreglo que pudiera comprometer el testimonio de esa dependencia. Esto no es una regla universal según la cual los creyentes deban rechazar toda remuneración o toda relación comercial. Es un ejemplo narrativo de cómo guardar la integridad cuando una ganancia aparentemente legítima podría torcer la lealtad o el testimonio.

blocks.en: Genesis 15:6 — Righteousness by Faith
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 15:6 — Justicia por Fe

blocks.en: When Abram struggles with the absence of an heir, God again speaks promise and points him toward descendants beyond his ability to count. Genesis then says, “And he believed in the LORD, and He accounted it to him for righteousness.” This verse becomes foundational in Romans 4 and Galatians 3. Abraham’s right standing with God is not presented as a wage earned by flawless performance. He believes God, and righteousness is credited to him; salvation is by grace through faith.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Abram lucha con la falta de un heredero, Dios vuelve a hablarle con una promesa y le señala una descendencia que él no podría contar. Entonces Génesis dice: «Y creyó a Jehová, y le fue contado por justicia». Este versículo llega a ser fundamental en Romanos 4 y Gálatas 3. La justicia de Abraham delante de Dios no se presenta como un salario ganado por un desempeño impecable. Abraham cree a Dios, y la justicia le es contada; la salvación es por gracia mediante la fe.

blocks.en: The Covenant Ceremony
blocks.es_reference: La Ceremonia del Pacto

blocks.en: Genesis 15 records a solemn covenant ceremony in which divided animals are prepared and, in the vision, the smoking oven and burning torch pass between the pieces. The striking feature is that God symbolically takes upon Himself the covenant commitment while Abram is in a deep sleep. The passage does not make Abraham irrelevant, because faith and obedience remain important throughout his life. But it grounds the promise in divine commitment. The future of the covenant finally depends upon the faithfulness of the God who made it.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 15 registra una solemne ceremonia de pacto en la que se preparan animales partidos por la mitad y, en la visión, un horno humeante y una antorcha de fuego pasan entre las piezas. Lo más llamativo es que Dios toma simbólicamente sobre sí el compromiso del pacto mientras Abram está sumido en un profundo sueño. El pasaje no hace irrelevante a Abraham, porque la fe y la obediencia siguen siendo importantes a lo largo de su vida. Pero fundamenta la promesa en el compromiso divino. En definitiva, el futuro del pacto depende de la fidelidad del Dios que lo hizo.

blocks.en: The Gospel Trajectory of Abraham’s Call
blocks.es_reference: La Trayectoria del Evangelio en el Llamado de Abraham

blocks.en: Paul says in Galatians 3 that Scripture “preached the gospel to Abraham beforehand,” citing the promise that all nations would be blessed in him. The statement does not mean Abraham possessed every later detail of New Testament revelation. It means the promise already contained the redemptive trajectory that reaches the nations through Christ. Abraham’s call therefore belongs directly to the gospel story. God’s purpose is not simply to create one favored family but through that family to advance blessing toward the world.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo dice en Gálatas 3 que la Escritura «predicó antes el evangelio a Abraham», y cita la promesa de que todas las naciones serían benditas en él. Esta declaración no significa que Abraham conociera cada detalle posterior de la revelación del Nuevo Testamento. Significa que la promesa ya contenía la trayectoria redentora que llega a las naciones por medio de Cristo. Por tanto, el llamado de Abraham forma parte directa de la historia del evangelio. El propósito de Dios no es simplemente crear una familia favorecida, sino hacer avanzar la bendición hacia el mundo por medio de esa familia.

blocks.en: Ministry Application
blocks.es_reference: Aplicación Ministerial

blocks.en: Abraham’s early story gives ministry a theology of calling rooted in grace. God calls people who have not earned His favor, asks for trust that becomes obedience, restores after failure, teaches generosity instead of anxious grasping, and turns blessing outward in service. At the same time, Abraham’s mistakes warn leaders not to confuse calling with infallibility. A person may genuinely follow God and still act fearfully or foolishly. The security of ministry must therefore rest not in constructing a heroic image of the servant but in the faithfulness of the God who calls.
blocks.es_reference: La primera parte de la historia de Abraham ofrece al ministerio una teología del llamamiento arraigada en la gracia. Dios llama a personas que no se han ganado su favor, pide una confianza que se convierte en obediencia, restaura después del fracaso, enseña la generosidad en lugar del afán de aferrarse, y orienta la bendición hacia afuera, hacia el servicio. Al mismo tiempo, los errores de Abraham advierten a los líderes que no confundan el llamamiento con la infalibilidad. Una persona puede seguir sinceramente a Dios y aun así actuar con temor o con insensatez. Por tanto, la seguridad del ministerio no debe descansar en construir una imagen heroica del siervo, sino en la fidelidad del Dios que llama.

blocks.en: Summary
blocks.es_reference: Resumen

blocks.en: Genesis 12–15 introduces Abraham as a man called by grace into a life of faith, obedience, worship, failure, restoration, courage, and covenant promise. The central actor remains God: He calls, promises, protects, reaffirms, credits righteousness through faith, and commits Himself to the covenant purpose. Abraham is blessed in order to become a blessing, and the horizon of his call includes all the families of the earth. What Babel tried to seize through self-made greatness, Abraham receives as gift; what humanity scattered in rebellion, God begins to address through a promise that ultimately reaches the nations in Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 12–15 presenta a Abraham como un hombre llamado por gracia a una vida de fe, obediencia, adoración, fracaso, restauración, valentía y promesa del pacto. El protagonista sigue siendo Dios: Él llama, promete, protege, reafirma, atribuye la justicia por medio de la fe y se compromete con el propósito del pacto. Abraham es bendecido para llegar a ser bendición, y el horizonte de su llamado incluye a todas las familias de la tierra. Lo que Babel intentó arrebatar mediante una grandeza fabricada por sí misma, Abraham lo recibe como don; lo que la humanidad dispersó en su rebelión, Dios comienza a remediarlo mediante una promesa que, en última instancia, llega a las naciones en Cristo.

mc.stem: What does Joshua 24 indicate about Abraham’s family background?
options: It was a line of priests serving God Most High
It came from the royal household of Egypt
It was known for faithful worship of the LORD in Ur
It was associated with the worship of other gods
mc.why: It was associated with the worship of other gods.

mc.stem: What does that background emphasize about Abraham’s call?
options: His family's religious heritage
Abram's own spiritual search
God’s gracious initiative
Abram's superior piety
mc.why: God’s gracious initiative.

mc.stem: What does God command Abram to do in Genesis 12?
options: Go down to Egypt to escape the famine
Build an ark and gather his household into it
Return to Ur and restore his father's altar
Leave and go to the land God will show him
mc.why: Leave and go to the land God will show him.

mc.stem: How does Abraham’s name contrast with Babel?
options: Both seek a name, but Abram works harder to build his
Abram seeks to make a name; Babel's builders avoid all fame
Babel seeks to make a name; God promises to make Abram’s name great
Babel's name is a gift from God; Abram must earn his own
mc.why: Babel seeks to make a name; God promises to make Abram’s name great.

mc.stem: Which three themes summarize the patriarchal promise?
options: A city, a tower, and a name
Kingship, temple, and priesthood
Wealth, health, and long life
Land, descendants, and blessing
mc.why: Land, descendants, and blessing.

mc.stem: Why is Abraham blessed?
options: Because he had earned God's favor in Ur
Because his family worshiped the LORD faithfully
So that he may enjoy private prosperity
So that he may become a blessing to others
mc.why: So that he may become a blessing to others.

mc.stem: How does Abram initially respond to God’s call?
options: He departs as the LORD spoke
He asks God for a sign first
He laughs in disbelief at the promise
He sends Lot ahead to explore
mc.why: He departs as the LORD spoke.

mc.stem: What do tents and altars portray?
options: Settled ownership and military strength in Canaan
Aimless wandering without direction or purpose
Pilgrimage and worshipful trust in God’s promise
Wealth and high social status among the nations
mc.why: Pilgrimage and worshipful trust in God’s promise.

mc.stem: What does the Egypt episode reveal?
options: God's grace means He approves Abram's deception
The man of faith can still fail through fear
Egypt was the land God had promised to Abram
The famine proves that God's promise has failed
mc.why: The man of faith can still fail through fear.

mc.stem: What does Abram do after returning from Egypt?
options: Returns to the altar and calls on the LORD
Settles permanently near Pharaoh's court
Builds a city and names it after himself
Offers Isaac on Mount Moriah
mc.why: Returns to the altar and calls on the LORD.

mc.stem: How should Lot be portrayed?
options: Simply as a villain who opposed Abram at every turn
With nuance: a righteous man who nevertheless makes dangerous choices
As Abram's son and the chosen heir of the promise
As an ideal example whose choices were consistently wise
mc.why: With nuance: a righteous man who nevertheless makes dangerous choices.

mc.stem: Why can Abram let Lot choose first?
options: He was already planning to return to Egypt
The Jordan plain looked dry and worthless to him
His future rests in God’s promise rather than visible advantage
Lot was the older and senior member of the family
mc.why: His future rests in God’s promise rather than visible advantage.

mc.stem: What does Genesis 14 show about faith?
options: Faith rests mainly on military skill and strength
Faith can be peaceable and still act courageously
Faith means staying passive while others suffer
Faith must avoid every dealing with kings
mc.why: Faith can be peaceable and still act courageously.

mc.stem: Who blesses Abram after the battle?
options: Melchizedek, priest of God Most High
The king of Sodom, ruler of the plain
Pharaoh, king of Egypt
Lot, his rescued nephew
mc.why: Melchizedek, priest of God Most High.

mc.stem: Why does Abram refuse the king of Sodom’s enrichment?
options: To give the entire spoil to Melchizedek instead
To guard the witness that his blessing comes from God
To obey a rule that believers must refuse all payment
To avoid provoking the king of Sodom's allies
mc.why: To guard the witness that his blessing comes from God.

mc.stem: What does Genesis 15:6 say about Abram?
options: He obeyed the commandments and so earned a righteous standing
He believed the LORD and it was accounted to him for righteousness
He laughed at the promise and was rebuked by the LORD
He offered a sacrifice and it was accepted as payment for sin
mc.why: He believed the LORD and it was accounted to him for righteousness.

mc.stem: How does Paul use Genesis 15:6?
options: To show righteousness is earned by Abraham's obedience
To limit the promise to Abraham's physical descendants
To teach righteousness by faith rather than earned wages
To teach that circumcision secures right standing
mc.why: To teach righteousness by faith rather than earned wages.

mc.stem: What is striking about the Genesis 15 covenant ceremony?
options: God symbolically assumes the covenant commitment
Abram alone walks between the pieces
Melchizedek presides as covenant priest
Abram pledges to keep the covenant flawlessly
mc.why: God symbolically assumes the covenant commitment.

mc.stem: According to Galatians 3, what was announced beforehand to Abraham?
options: The gospel trajectory of blessing to the nations
The law later given at Mount Sinai
Every detail of New Testament revelation
The coming destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
mc.why: The gospel trajectory of blessing to the nations.

mc.stem: Who remains the central actor in Abraham’s call?
options: Melchizedek, the priest-king of Salem
Abraham, the self-made hero of faith
Lot, whose choices drive the story
The God who calls, promises, and keeps covenant
mc.why: The God who calls, promises, and keeps covenant.
